mainEntity.name: How do I scale a recipe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the servings you want by the servings in the original recipe to get a multiplier, then multiply every ingredient by it. To go from 4 to 10 servings, multiply by 2.5.

mainEntity.name: Why is weight better than cups for baking?

acceptedAnswer.text: A cup of flour can weigh 120 g or more than 150 g depending on how you scoop it. Weighing ingredients removes that variation, which is why bakers use grams.
It expresses each ingredient as a percentage of the flour weight, which is always 100%. A dough with 700 g water to 1,000 g flour has a hydration of 70%.

mainEntity.name: How many grams are in a cup?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the ingredient: about 120 g of all-purpose flour, 200 g of granulated sugar, 227 g of butter and 237 g of water. Use the ingredient type in the tool for the right figure.

mainEntity.name: Do baking times change when I scale a recipe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. A larger or deeper batch takes longer, a smaller one less, and pan size changes how it browns. Use time and doneness cues rather than scaling time directly.
